pll2d12c2-d1e3514.summary: Notes that some Fathers who searched God's words seem to have written contrary things about this.

pll2d12c2-d1e3517.summary: Reports that some held all was created at once in matter and form, as Augustine seems to have thought.
claims: Augustine seems to hold simultaneous creation.

pll2d12c2-d1e3523.summary: Reports that others held that rude, unformed matter, a mixture of the four elements, was created first, and then over six days the kinds of bodies were formed from it; Gregory, Jerome, Bede, and others prefer this, and it fits Genesis better.
claims: Matter was created first, then formed over six days.

pl-l2d12c2.summary: Notes that the Fathers seem to have written as if contrary: some, including Augustine, held all was created simultaneously in matter and form; others, Gregory, Jerome, Bede, and many, held that unformed matter was created first and then formed over six days, which seems to fit Genesis better.
claims: Augustine seems to hold that all was created simultaneously in matter and form.
Gregory, Jerome, Bede, and others hold that matter was formed over six days.
The six-day view fits Genesis better.
